templateVars.title: Using template variables
templateVars.description: Custom response page content supports {{placeholder}} placeholders. coreX replaces them with live request values when the page is served. For example, adding {{requestId}} to a WAF or other block page lets you correlate the event with the full coreX log.

vars.rateLimitWindow: rate limit window in seconds (e.g. "60"), available on 429 rate limit pages
vars.rateLimitDuration: block duration in seconds (e.g. "300"), 0 if no block duration

templateVars.advanced: Any other {{name}} is treated as a transaction variable %[var(txn.name)]. You can also use HAProxy sample-fetch syntax directly, such as %[req.hdr(X-Custom)].

ja4.title: JA4 TLS Fingerprinting
ja4.description: Computes JA4 TLS client fingerprints from the ClientHello. Used by Security Rules referencing http.request.ja4. Disabling will automatically disable any security rules that reference JA4; re-enabling will turn them back on.

reqFp.title: HTTP Request Fingerprinting
reqFp.description: Computes a 17-field HTTP request/response fingerprint stored in txn.req_fp. Available for custom log formats and headers via %[var(txn.req_fp)].
reqFp.requiredByApiArmor: Required by API Armor. Disabling will also prevent API Armor from being enabled.
reqFp.failedToSave: Failed to save request fingerprinting setting.

parseBody.enable: Parse request bodies for fingerprint params
parseBody.description: When enabled, form-urlencoded and JSON request bodies are buffered and parsed to extract parameter keys, types, and lengths into the fingerprint's param fields. This adds body buffering overhead to every matching POST/PUT/PATCH. When API Armor is enabled on a listener, it handles body buffering automatically and this setting has no additional effect. Bodies larger than the configured max inspection size are either rejected with HTTP 413 (if enforcement is enabled) or skip body parsing — body params are returned as nil (param keys/types = nil, param lengths = 0) and the request proceeds normally.
parseBody.failedToSave: Failed to save body parsing setting.

maxBodyBytes.label: Max body inspection size
maxBodyBytes.description: Maximum request body size (in bytes) that will be buffered and parsed for fingerprint params. Bodies larger than this are either rejected (if enforcement is enabled) or skip body parsing. Default is 1048576 (1 MB).
maxBodyBytes.failedToSave: Failed to save max body size.

enforceMaxBody.description: When enabled, requests with bodies larger than the max inspection size are rejected with HTTP 413. When disabled, oversized bodies skip body parsing and the request proceeds normally (body params are returned as nil).
enforceMaxBody.enabled: Enforcement enabled — oversized bodies are rejected with 413.
enforceMaxBody.disabled: Enforcement disabled — oversized bodies skip body parsing.

compression.title: Response Compression
compression.description: Enables brotli and zstd response compression algorithms via the haproxy-compression Rust Lua module. When enabled, the algorithm becomes selectable per-backend in the backend editor. gzip and deflate are always available (native) and do not require these toggles.

diskCache.title: Disk Cache
diskCache.description: Enables file-backed disk caching for large objects. When enabled, the disk cache option becomes available per-backend in the Caching page. Memory cache (coreX native) is always available and does not require this toggle.
diskCache.enable: Enable disk cache for large file caching
diskCache.failedToSave: Failed to save disk cache setting.

respTransform.title: Response Transforms
respTransform.description: Enables response body rewriting, injection, and bidirectional mask/unmask via the haproxy-resp-transform Rust Lua module. When enabled, transform rules become configurable per-backend on the Response Transforms page. Mask mode uses Valkey (tokenize) or AES-256-GCM (encrypt) for sensitive data protection.
respTransform.failedToSave: Failed to save response transforms setting.

img2Webp.title: Image Conversion (WebP)
img2Webp.description: Enables on-the-fly JPEG/PNG/GIF to WebP conversion module. When enabled, per-backend image conversion settings become available on the Backends page. The filter performs content negotiation based on the Accept header — no rewrite rules or src-link replacement needed. Converted responses include Vary: Accept for correct caching.
img2Webp.failedToSave: Failed to save image conversion setting.

apiArmor.title: API Armor
apiArmor.description: Enables API & GraphQL protection: GraphQL query parsing, JSON schema validation, JWT/API-key auth validation, and multi-dimensional behavioral profiling. When enabled, conditional body buffering is activated on API Armor-enabled listeners, and req_fp v2 parses request bodies (merging body params into the fingerprint). Configure per-listener via the listener's API Armor option. Full settings available on the API Armor page.
apiArmor.failedToSave: Failed to save API Armor setting.

riskScoring.title: Risk Scoring
riskScoring.subtitle: Risk rules accumulate a per-request risk score (0-99) consumed by Security Rules.

riskScoring.helpDescription: Each matching risk rule adds or subtracts points from a per-request raw score. The total positive points across all enabled rules is capped at 99 (the budget above). Scores are computed per ruleset — Security Rules can reference risk.score (default), risk.human.score, risk.api.score, etc. Each ruleset also exposes risk.<slug>.rules_hit (matched rule names), risk.<slug>.rules_hit_count (int count), and risk.<slug>.hit_density (percentage of rules matched).
riskScoring.helpDensity: When density amplification is enabled, bonus points are added based on how broadly the request hit rules in the ruleset: final = raw_score + floor(hit_density × weight), capped at 99. This means a request matching many low-point rules (e.g. a scanner) can still produce a high score. Adjust the weight using the slider on the right — higher weight amplifies breadth more aggressively.
riskScoring.helpExampleCode:
risk.score > 60 → Block
risk.api.score > 30 and risk.api.rules_hit_count > 3 → Challenge
risk.rules_hit contains "IP in blocklist" → Block

helpCard.title: How Risk Scoring Works
helpCard.body: Each matching risk rule adds or subtracts points from a per-request score (clamped 0-99). Scores are computed per ruleset — Security Rules can reference risk.score (default ruleset), risk.human.score, risk.api.score, risk.mobile.score, etc. Each ruleset also exposes risk.<slug>.rules_hit (matched rule names) and risk.<slug>.rules_hit_count (int count of matched rules).

rateLimits.title: Rate Limits
rateLimits.responseCodeDescription: Blocks clients that receive more than {{events}} responses with status {{statusCode}} within {{window}}s. The counter increments in the response phase (after the backend replies), so only actual backend responses are counted.

tooltips.name: Display name for this rate limit.
tooltips.listener: Listener to apply the rate limit to, or all listeners.
tooltips.type: Trigger type: basic, advanced expression, WAF-triggered, or response-code based.
tooltips.events: Number of events allowed in the window before the action is triggered.
tooltips.windowSeconds: Time window for the event counter.
tooltips.burst: Number of excess requests allowed before the first blocking decision. Defaults to 0 (no burst).
tooltips.durationSeconds: Only applies to the Tarpit action. How long a client remains blocked (held open then dropped) after the limit is exceeded. Ignored for block/allow/log actions.
tooltips.action: Action to take when the limit is exceeded. Block: deny the request immediately with the configured status code. Allow: let the request through (use to exempt matching clients from other rate limits). Log: count and log the request but do not block. Tarpit: hold the connection open without responding, then drop it, and keep the client blocked for the configured Duration. Challenge: redirect the client to a CAPTCHA challenge page; solved challenges bypass rate limiting for the configured TTL.
tooltips.suppressRequestLog: Do not write the underlying request to the access log.
tooltips.expression: HAProxy stick-table / ACL expression that controls when the counter increments.
tooltips.advancedResponseCode: HTTP status returned to blocked clients.
tooltips.urlPath: Path or pattern used in the expression.
tooltips.userAgent: User-Agent string or pattern used in the expression.
tooltips.wafThreshold: Number of WAF events within the window that triggers blocking.
tooltips.wafWindow: Time window for WAF event counting.
tooltips.wafBlockDuration: How long the client is blocked after the threshold is exceeded.
tooltips.matchStatusCode: Backend status code that increments the counter, e.g. `404`.
tooltips.blockStatusCode: Status code returned to the client when the limit is hit.
tooltips.rateKey: Dimension to count requests by: source IP, user ID, header, path, or ASN (requires MaxMind ASN database). Only basic, advanced, and WAF-triggered types support non-src keys; response-code always counts by source IP.
tooltips.rateHeader: Header containing the user ID or API key when Rate Key is set to header/user_id.

modal.name: Name
modal.responsePageQueryHelp: Parameters are set on the request before the response page is returned. Use HAProxy sample-fetch syntax such as %[url_param(message)] or %[query].
modal.responsePageNote: This redirect will return the selected custom response page content directly instead of performing a URL redirect.

tooltips.name: Display name for this redirect.
tooltips.listeners: Listeners this redirect applies to; none means all.
tooltips.source: Path prefix or regex to match.
tooltips.customResponsePage: Return an error page directly instead of redirecting.
tooltips.target: Destination URL when not using a custom response page.
tooltips.code: HTTP status code for the redirect (301, 302, 307, 308).
tooltips.responsePageQueryString: Query parameters set on the request before serving the custom page.
tooltips.type: Match type: permanent (301), temporary (302), or regex.
tooltips.preserveQuery: Carry the original query string into the redirect target.
tooltips.rewriteListeners: Listeners this rewrite applies to; none means all.
tooltips.hostMatch: Optional Host header value to restrict the rewrite to.
tooltips.regex: Regular expression matching the path (and query when type is `both`).
tooltips.rewriteType: Rewrite the path, the query string, or both.

responseTransforms.title: Response Transforms
responseTransforms.description: Rewrite, inject, or mask response body content per-backend. Mask rules also unmask tokens in request bodies (bidirectional). Requires the Response Transform module enabled in Global Options.

tooltips.name: Display name for this response transform rule.
tooltips.backends: Backends this rule applies to; none means all backends.
tooltips.transformType: replace = regex find/replace in response body; inject = insert content at an anchor; mask = detect sensitive data and replace with tokens.
tooltips.contentTypes: Comma-separated MIME type prefixes to match (e.g. text/html, application/json). Empty = all content types.
tooltips.maxBodySize: Skip transformation if response body exceeds this size (bytes). Default 1MB.
tooltips.findRegex: Regex pattern to find in the response body. Uses Rust regex syntax (linear-time, no backtracking).
tooltips.injectString: Content to inject at the anchor position.
tooltips.injectPosition: Where to inject relative to the regex match: before, after, or replace the match.
tooltips.maskMode: detector = use built-in PII detector; regex = use custom regex.
tooltips.detector: Built-in PII detector: email, phone, ssn, credit_card, ip.
tooltips.tokenMode: tokenize = store token→original in Valkey with TTL; encrypt = AES-256-GCM encrypt with env key.
tooltips.tokenPrefix: Prefix for generated tokens (e.g. TOK_ or ENC_). Used to find tokens in request bodies for unmasking.
tooltips.tokenTtl: TTL in seconds for tokenize mode. After expiry, original data is unrecoverable.
tooltips.encryptKeyEnv: Name of the environment variable holding the AES-256 key (min 32 bytes). The key itself is never stored in the DB.
tooltips.detokenizeQuery: When enabled, tokens from this rule are also resolved back to original values in URL query strings on incoming requests (e.g. tokens in href links). Note: tokens in URLs may appear in access logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
